# Psalm 109 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** To-the-choirmaster. Of-David. A-psalm. O-God-of my-praise do-not be-silent,

**2** For mouth-of the-wicked and-mouth-of deceit against-me they-have-opened; they-have-spoken to-me with-tongue-of falsehood.

**3** And-words-of hatred they-have-surrounded-me, and-they-fight-me without-cause.

**4** In-return-for my-love they-accuse-me, and-I am-prayer.

**5** And-they-set upon-me evil for-good, and-hatred for-my-love.

**6** Set over-him a-wicked-one, and-an-accuser let-stand at-his-right-hand.

**7** When-he-is-judged let-him-go-out guilty, and-his-prayer let-it-become sin.

**8** Let-be his-days few; his-office let-take another.

**9** Let-be his-children fatherless, and-his-wife a-widow.

**10** And-let-wander his-children and-beg, and-let-them-seek from-their-ruins.

**11** Let-ensnare the-creditor all which to-him, and-let-plunder strangers his-labor.

**12** Let-there-not be to-him one-extending kindness, and-let-there-not be one-being-gracious to-his-fatherless-children.

**13** Let-be his-posterity for-cutting-off; in-generation following let-be-blotted-out their-name.

**14** Let-be-remembered the-iniquity-of his-fathers to YHWH, and-sin-of his-mother let-not be-blotted-out.

**15** Let-them-be before YHWH continually, and-let-him-cut-off from-the-earth their-memory,

**16** Because not he-remembered to-do kindness, and-he-pursued a-man afflicted and-needy and-broken-of heart to-put-to-death.

**17** And-he-loved cursing and-it-came to-him; and-not he-delighted in-blessing and-it-was-far from-him.

**18** And-he-clothed-himself cursing as-his-garment, and-it-came like-water into-his-inward-parts, and-like-oil into-his-bones.

**19** Let-it-be to-him like-a-garment he-wraps-in, and-like-a-belt he-binds continually.

**20** This the-wages-of my-accusers from YHWH, and-those-speaking evil against my-soul.

**21** And-you O-YHWH Lord, deal with-me for-sake-of your-name; because good your-steadfast-love deliver-me.

**22** For afflicted and-needy I-am, and-my-heart is-pierced within-me.

**23** Like-a-shadow when-it-lengthens I-go; I-am-shaken-off like-the-locust.

**24** My-knees stumble from-fasting, and-my-flesh has-grown-lean without-fatness.

**25** And-I have-become a-reproach to-them; they-see-me they-shake their-head.

**26** Help-me O-YHWH my-God; save-me according-to your-steadfast-love.

**27** And-let-them-know that this your-hand; you O-YHWH have-done-it.

**28** They-curse and-you bless; they-have-risen and-they-are-ashamed, and-your-servant will-rejoice.

**29** Let-be-clothed my-accusers with-disgrace, and-let-them-wrap-themselves as-a-robe their-shame.

**30** I-will-give-thanks to-YHWH greatly with-my-mouth, and-in-midst-of many I-will-praise-him.

**31** For he-stands at-right-hand-of the-needy, to-save from-those-judging his-soul.

---
## EMET Literal Notes

- **109:4**: 'And-I am-prayer' (va'ani tefillah) — extraordinary: the psalmist doesn't just pray; he becomes prayer itself.

- **109:6-19**: The most extended imprecation in the Psalter. Debate: is David quoting his enemies' curses against him (vv. 6-19), or directing his own curses against them?

- **109:8**: Quoted in Acts 1:20 regarding Judas: 'his office let-take another' — applied to the apostolic vacancy.

— EMET
